policy._note: Decided by /repo-story on 2026-08-25 and proven, not inferred: the tag resolves, is lightweight (no tag-object trap), clones cleanly at 474a349a, is an ancestor of main, and is 6 days old with main 341 commits ahead. Pinned rather than default-branch so the map, the screenshots and the enrichment all describe a commit that still exists later, which matters because a full enrichment is a real amount of the weekly allowance and a moving target cannot be compared against a later run. NOT latest-tag: version-sort on this repo returns vsda-v1.39.1, which is not a VS Code release. See docs/publication/repo-stories/vscode.md.

budget._note: 200.0 is a runaway stop, not a budget. Owner decision 2026-08-24: a subject is analysed and enriched to the best this system can do, or not at all, so there is no spending target to hit and a ceiling that truncates a run is worse than no ceiling. The previous 45.0 sat INSIDE the run's own projected $38-79 bracket and would have stopped the ladder partway, leaving the partial enrichment posture that --profile enriched rejects. Dollars here are API-equivalent units reported by the claude CLI and metered against the owner's Claude Max subscription; no card is charged, which is why the figure is a tripwire rather than a budget. What actually needs watching is the share of the weekly subscription allowance one run consumes: see scripts/usage-budget.py. max_wall_minutes raised to 240 for the same reason, so a slow run finishes rather than being killed mid-ladder.

enrichment._note: min_rounds 1 is the Wave 1 forced-iteration decision: on the first subjects the determination runs an improvement round even when it believes the map is done, with a genuine reasoned target, so the tuning that later decides 'iterate or not' is learned rather than guessed. A binding is 'source:model'; 'source:auto' leaves the model unpinned so that source routes the call itself. See docs/publication/ENRICHMENT-ENGINE.md sections 2 and 3.
